epic.title: Blocking: listed outlets and adult sites, block with "open anyway"
epic.description:
The BBC, the Daily Mail, ITV and further outlets Phil approves (each with a reason from the four allowed sources) are blocked from his life, everything from them and not only news, on the one network-wide DNS filter from E.net, with an "open anyway" page: quick for news, a 10-minute wait for adult sites, growing after a heavy week. Per-person profiles from the start (Phil, Kirsty unfiltered for news, guests, a future child); the same filter on his phones away from home; bypasses closed on his devices; built-in feeds, YouTube, search, Alexa, podcasts and emails swept; shared TVs only as Kirsty agrees. A weekly digest from sources he chooses replaces the news, and an owner-only count sits in the Sunday close-out.

## Order
The outlet research (block.01), Kirsty's TV conversation (block.02) and the licence note (block.15) start at once. Profiles (block.03) wait for net.03 (and sub.06 if the filter is on Substrate). Lists (block.04) after block.01 and block.03; then the block page design and build (block.05), the count (block.20). Device work after the profiles: bypasses (block.06), phones away from home (block.07), social limits (block.17). Channel sweeps after block.01: emails and apps (block.08), YouTube (block.10), search (block.11), Alexa (block.12), podcasts (block.13); news feeds off (block.09) any time. Sky Glass research (block.14) after block.02, then shared TVs (block.16). Digest (block.18) after sub.14; official alerts (block.19) any time. Test run (block.21), then the 30-day done check (block.23); the yearly review (block.22) from the date block.04 goes live.

## Done means
Thirty days without seeing a listed outlet unless Phil chose to.

## Flags
None from the brief. Design question carried on block.05: an HTTPS block page needs a trusted root certificate on each device.

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs.

Each row lists the outlet's domains and apps (everything from the outlet, not only news, so the BBC row includes iPlayer, Sport and Sounds). The result is a checklist of proposed outlets with approve or decline per row for Phil; nothing is blocked from it until he ticks.

## Why
Section 9 answers 1, 2 and 5: a research ticket proposes outlets with a reason each; he approves each one. 9b: everything from a listed outlet is blocked, not only news.

## Done looks like
A table on the ticket (outlet, domains and apps, reason, source with date) and Phil's approve or decline on every row.

## Unlocks

tickets.title: The block page: next thing from Mycelium with Start, this week's count, a saved quote; "open anyway" quick for news, a 10-minute wait for adult sites
tickets.description:
## What
Claude designs, then builds, the block page in Mycelium. It shows Phil's next thing with a Start button, how many times he has landed this week, and one of his saved quotes. "Open anyway" is quick for news and has a 10-minute wait for adult sites; after a week of many open-anyways the wait grows the next week. Opening calls the filter's API to allow that site on that device for a set time. **Design first:** a DNS filter cannot show a page for an HTTPS site unless a root certificate is trusted on each device, and HSTS sites will not even allow a click-through (dossiers/block.md section 3.1). Claude writes the three options (a private root CA on Phil's own devices only; no CA, with "open anyway" in Mycelium and a PC browser extension; a hosted filter's branded page and CA) with their risks for Phil to choose, and builds only the chosen one.

## Why
9b: the block page shows his next thing with Start, this week's count and a saved quote; open anyway quick for news, a 10-minute wait for adult sites, and the wait grows after a week of many.

## Done looks like
Phil's choice of option recorded; the page built, landing on a listed site from his PC shows it, open anyway works with the right wait per list, and the count updates.

## Unlocks
block.20 (the weekly count reads the open-anyways), block.23 (done check).

## Depends on
block.04 (the lists to block against).

## Flag
None from the brief. Design question for Phil: whether a private root certificate on his own phone and PC is acceptable (dossier section 5).

## Red team
- Finding 15: The Mycelium content is fetched only with the device's own session or device token; the unauthenticated block page shows the count and the quote only. No public endpoint.

tickets.title: Weekly count in the Sunday close-out: hits per list, open-anyways, owner-only; the Boys raise a bad week bluntly
tickets.description:
## What
Claude adds to the Sunday close-out an owner-only count: hits per list from the filter's logs, how many times Phil opened anyway, per list. A week over a threshold (Phil sets it) has the Boys raise it bluntly and ask why, and lengthens next week's open-anyway wait. Never on the wall, never shared.

## Why
Section 9 answers 24 and 25, and 9b: a weekly count in the Sunday close-out, owner-only; a week with many open-anyways is raised bluntly and the wait grows.

## Done looks like
The close-out shows the counts to Phil only; a staged heavy week triggers the Boys' message and a longer wait.

## Unlocks
block.23 (done check reads the counts).

## Depends on
block.05 (the open-anyway records).

A table of device, profile and the three results, all as intended.

After the test run passes, Phil keeps a 30-day watch: Claude reads the filter logs and the open-anyway records; any listed outlet seen without an open-anyway is a gap to fix. On day 30 Phil confirms he has not seen a listed outlet unless he chose to.

Day 30 reached with no unchosen sighting, or each gap fixed and the 30 days restarted.
